overclaims: Contemporary primary sources document all three kinds of problem: factual errors, substantial tool-use failures, and behavior changes between monthly versions.
checks.note: The excerpt, proposition, criteria, axis/outcome and citations are all fine. The problem is the rationale's 'behavior changes between monthly versions'. The only drift evidence (e3) compares March and June 2023 versions, about three months apart. It does not show changes from one month to the next, so the sentence overstates the cadence on exactly the point Marcus made ('month to month'). Suggested wording: 'behavior changes between dated model versions (March vs June 2023)'.

overclaims: Capability and safety improvements were real; they are compatible with Marcus’s explicit acknowledgment that scaling had helped in some ways.
Anthropic reported practical capability gains and improved safety measurements.
checks.note: e1, e2 and the outcome hold up. But e3's frozen text only has benchmark gains in capability, plus Anthropic saying it 'heard from our users' that Claude is 'less likely to produce harmful outputs'. No safety measurement appears in the frozen evidence. So 'improved safety measurements' (e3 explanation) is unsupported, and 'safety improvements were real' presents a user-reported claim from a vendor announcement as established fact. Capability gains are supported.
